Briefings in Bioinformatics.title: Correction of the cytosine deamination artifacts in FFPE-based sequencing experiments
Briefings in Bioinformatics.abstract: AbstractFormalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues remain an essential resource for molecular studies, yet formalin-induced cytosine deamination introduces characteristic C > T/G > A artifacts that compromise the accuracy of next-generation sequencing analyses. Numerous computational methods and enzymatic DNA repair strategies have been proposed to reduce these artifacts, but no systematic comparison across tools and experimental conditions exists. Here, we evaluate the performance of seven computational approaches (SOBDetector, Ideafix, MicroSEC, FFPolish, DeepOmics FFPE/FFPE-PLUS, FFPErase) together with the NEBNext® FFPE DNA Repair Mix v2, a multi-enzyme repair system applied during DNA preparation. Using three independent datasets, one based on whole genome sequencing (CGCI-BL) and two on whole exome sequencing (TCGA-PC and SUT-LUAD, the latter containing enzymatically repaired samples), and matched fresh-frozen samples as the gold standard, we assess precision, sensitivity, and artifact reduction efficiency across all methods. We further examine the potential synergy between enzymatic repair and post-sequencing computational filtering. Our results provide practical guidelines for FFPE artifact correction and demonstrate that enzymatic treatment provides the best results, while among the computational methods, FFPErase offers the most robust reduction of cytosine deamination artifacts while maximizing the retention of true somatic variants.

Briefings in Bioinformatics.title: Integration of single-cell multi-omic data with graph-based topic modelling
Briefings in Bioinformatics.abstract: AbstractRecent advances in single-cell biology enable the profiling of multiple molecular layers, such as the transcriptome, epigenome, and surface proteins, within a single cell. Tackling the complexity of these data from multiple perspectives allows researchers to gain the most comprehensive insights into cellular biological properties. Here, we propose a graph-based topic modelling method called bionSBM. Our method leverages well-known community-detection methods for multipartite graphs and the interpretability of topic modelling to cluster and explain high-dimensional, sparse, and noisy single-cell matrices. We applied our algorithm to paired single-cell multi-omics data, such as 10X Multiome, SHARE-seq, and CITE-seq. We showed that it achieves superior performance compared with state-of-the-art methods for ground-truth label retrieval, with high specificity and distinct biological interpretability.

Briefings in Bioinformatics.title: Koinetic: a graph-based distance as a new ecological metric for microbial community differential analysis
Briefings in Bioinformatics.abstract: AbstractPhylogeny-aware beta diversity measures are essential in microbiome research, yet widely used metrics such as UniFrac and its variants rely on independent branch-length contributions and do not satisfy the Euclidean property, leading to distortions in ordination and kernel-based tests. These limitations underscore the need for a distance that is both phylogenetically coherent and geometrically valid. We introduce the Koinos Kinetic Distance (Koinetic), a phylogeny-aware dissimilarity that views microbial communities as interconnected assemblies rather than isolated taxa. ”Koinos” emphasizes collective evaluation, while ”kinetic” reflects how differences propagate dynamically across ecological networks and phylogenetic lineages. Koinetic leverages a graph Laplacian–based kernel to weight community differences by shared phylogeny, capturing ecological connectivity and clade relatedness. This design ensures Euclidean validity and enables seamless integration with kernel-based methods as well as geometry-preserving ordination. Controlled simulations and analyses of eight microbiome datasets spanning diverse body sites, disease contexts, and microbial profiling modalities demonstrate Koinetic’s broad applicability. Compared with classical and phylogenetic metrics, including weighted, unweighted, and generalized UniFrac, unweighted Koinetic can improve power for phylogenetically localized prevalence shifts in the simulated settings, while weighted Koinetic performs comparably with weighted and generalized UniFrac under abundance-driven signals. Koinetic also shows strong performance in PERMANOVA and MiRKAT analyses assessing associations between microbial community composition and host phenotypes. Koinetic thus provides a general foundation for phylogeny-aware analysis, with a consistent geometric basis for visualization and statistical inference.

Briefings in Bioinformatics.title: ESGI: efficient splitting of generic indices in single-cell sequencing data
Briefings in Bioinformatics.abstract: AbstractSingle-cell sequencing technologies increasingly rely on complex nucleotide barcoding schemes to encode cellular identities, experimental conditions, and molecular modalities within a single experiment. While demultiplexing, alignment, and unique molecular identifier (UMI)-based quantification form the core preprocessing steps that transform raw sequencing reads into analyzable single-cell data, existing pipelines are often tightly coupled to specific experimental designs and typically assume fixed barcode positions and substitution-only error models. As a result, many assays employing combinatorial, variable-length, or multimodal barcoding designs require custom, hard-coded preprocessing solutions that are difficult to generalize and maintain. Here, we present efficient splitting of generic indices (ESGI), a flexible framework for demultiplexing and processing single-cell sequencing data with arbitrary barcode architectures. ESGI operates directly on raw FASTQ files using a generic barcode pattern specification, supports barcode matching with insertions and deletions via Levenshtein distance, accommodates variable-length barcodes, and provides detailed quality metrics for barcode assignment. ESGI optionally integrates genome alignment via STAR and performs feature quantification and UMI collapsing to generate cell-by-feature count matrices. ESGI is well documented and readily applicable to novel single-cell experiments. We demonstrate the versatility of ESGI across six datasets spanning four distinct single-cell technologies, including combinatorial indexing–based transcriptomic and multimodal assays, feature barcode-based protein measurements, and spatial barcoding data. Across these applications, ESGI robustly demultiplexes complex barcode designs that are not natively supported by existing pipelines, while producing results comparable with established workflows where applicable. ESGI provides a general solution for processing a wide range of barcoded single-cell sequencing data, enabling rapid adoption and analysis of emerging experimental designs.

Water Research.title: Uncovering the potential of zero-valent aluminum/persulfate: Organophosphorus wastewater treatment via oxidation followed by pH-controlled coagulation for phosphorus recovery.
Water Research.abstract: Organophosphorus pollutants (OPs) in wastewater present as both toxic pollutants and carriers of finite phosphorus (P) resources. To sustainably mitigate OPs pollution and recover P resources, this study explored the potential of zero-valent aluminum activated persulfate (ZVAl/PDS) for integrated OPs degradation and resource recovery. The system generated more hydroxyl radicals, sulfate radicals, and singlet oxygen under acidic conditions, benefiting the degradation process. Owing to the simultaneous release of aqueous Al and P during the reaction, the system triggered coagulation under neutral conditions to accelerate the solidification of P. Building upon these insights, a two-stage ZVAl/PDS configuration was designed to reconcile OPs degradation and phosphate release with P solidification. This two-stage design enabled efficient total phosphorus (TP) removal from wastewaters containing different OPs. Phytotoxicity assays further demonstrated reduced toxicity of the treated effluent to mung bean seedlings. In continuous-flow treatment of 3 L of real OPs-containing wastewater, the system reduced TP concentrations from 20.64 mg PO43-/L in the influent to 0.34 mg PO43-/L in the final effluent. Furthermore, strategies for Al and P recovery and reuse were also evaluated, with an economic assessment highlighting the potential value of the recovered products. Ultimately, this study provided a sustainable approach to OPs wastewater treatment that integrated pollution control with P recovery, advancing the mechanistic understanding of the underlying processes.

Water Research.title: Vortex-regulated transport enables rapid microalgae harvesting in a sponge-inspired flow system.
Water Research.abstract: Harmful algal blooms threaten aquatic ecosystems and drinking water safety, creating an urgent need for rapid and environmentally compatible biomass removal. Although adsorption-based harvesting offers strong cell-surface affinity, its practical performance is often constrained by inefficient mass transfer, transport blockage, and early breakthrough under flow. Here, we develop a sea-sponge-inspired flow system that couples hydrodynamic regulation with cationic-fiber adsorption for rapid microalgae harvesting. Inspired by the hierarchical skeleton of Euplectella aspergillum, the system integrates an outer 3D-printed helical lattice with an internal matrix of amine-functionalized poly(lactic acid) fibers. The helical architecture generates vortex-enhanced mixing, low-velocity retention zones, and longer cell residence within the structure, while the cationic fibrous matrix provides accessible binding interfaces for negatively charged algal cells. At an initial cell concentration of approximately 107 cells mL-1, the sponge-inspired system achieved 87.8% removal within 1 h, compared with 10.9% for the fiber-only sorption control. Numerical simulations showed that the helical ridges reorganized intracavity velocity and pressure fields and increased particle retention, consistent with the experimental kinetic enhancement. The process preserved cell morphology and photosynthetic function, caused no detectable increase in the release of intracellular organic compounds, and enabled recovery of the captured biomass, along with the regeneration and reuse of the PLA-PEI fibers. Continuous-flow experiments and validation in natural surface water further demonstrated rapid and robust microalgae removal. These results establish transport-oriented structural design as an effective strategy for overcoming mass-transfer limitations in adsorption-based algal harvesting.

Water Research.title: Understanding morphological effects of green landscapes on watershed water quality across China.
Water Research.abstract: Water quality remains a major concern in China and other rapidly developing countries. Green vegetation regulates pollutant transport and watershed water quality through rainfall interception, infiltration, and runoff convergence. However, most studies rely on green space proportion or numerical landscape indices, with limited attention to explicit morphological units. Using 3646 monitoring stations across nine major Chinese basins from 2021 to 2025, we constructed watershed-scale Water Quality Index (WQI), applied Morphological Spatial Pattern Analysis (MSPA), and combined machine learning, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), generalized additive models (GAMs), and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). We found that: (1) WQI was generally higher in western and southern China and lower in eastern and northern China, with the Yellow, Songliao, Hai, and Huai River basins forming contiguous low-WQI clusters; (2) across all four seasons, MSP variables consistently explained WQI better than traditional landscape indices, increasing R² by 3.86%-6.08% and contributing 23.8%-31.9% of total model explanation; and (3) green landscape morphology showed clear nonlinear relationships with WQI. Core (continuous green interiors) showed the clearest positive relationship, whereas other MSP types showed peaks or turning points, with favorable associations within specific proportional ranges that weakened or became negative beyond them. PLS-SEM further identified a common "Topography → MSP → WQI" pathway across the four low-WQI hotspot basins, while direct and indirect pathways differed among basins. These findings support a shift from green space area control toward morphology-oriented watershed management.

Water Research.title: Sulfonate-enriching coating technique for nanofiltration membranes to enhance water permeation and removal of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances.
Water Research.abstract: The removal of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) from contaminated water sources can be significantly enhanced by adopting water treatment using nanofiltration (NF) membranes in drinking water applications. This study aimed to develop a sulfonate-enriching membrane surface coating technique to achieve high rejection of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) while preserving water permeance. Optimization of the surface coating technique involved optimizing the number of polyethylenimine (PEI) and poly(sodium 4-styrenesulfonate) (PSS) coats and different types of chemical treatments before and after the surface coating process. Notably, the triple-coated NF membrane pre-treated with NaOH exhibited a 15-24 % increase in the rejection of PFOA and PFOS, and its permeance was 15 % greater than that of an uncoated NF membrane. Characterization of the membranes indicated that the improved PFOA and PFOS rejection was likely due to the reduced pore size and increased electrostatic repulsion from the denser sulfonate groups in the polyamide separation layer of the NF membrane. The practicality of the developed NF membranes was demonstrated by the significant mitigation of membrane fouling during the treatment of typical surface water (dam water) and heavily contaminated water (simulated by primary wastewater effluent). The findings of this study highlight the potential of sulfonate-functionalized membrane surfaces to enhance PFOA and PFOS rejection, decrease the fouling tendency of NF membranes, and improve membrane permeability.

Microbiological Research.title: Genomic and functional analysis of the endophytic Flavobacterium johnsoniae UMJL46B reveals integrated growth-promotion strategies in Triticum aestivum.
Microbiological Research.abstract: Members of the genus Flavobacterium are abundant in the wheat endosphere; however, their functional roles in plant systems remain largely unresolved. In this study 11 endophytic Flavobacterium strains were isolated and evaluated for their effects on Triticum aestivum. Plant growth promotion assays revealed contrasting responses, ranging from growth inhibition to growth promotion. Among these strains, UMJL46B consistently exhibited plant growth promoting effects, including increases in shoot biomass (21%) as well as a notable increase in the number of lateral roots (84%). Whole genome sequencing confirmed that UMJL46B belongs to the F. johnsoniae species and revealed multiple plant associated functional traits, including genes involved in phytohormone biosynthesis, nutrient metabolism, stress tolerance, and volatile organic compound emission, as well as a putative cytochrome P450 associated with gibberellin biosynthesis. Functional assays validated these predictions. UMJL46B produced tryptophan-dependent indole-3-acetic acid, which correlated with modifications in root system architecture, including a 24% increase in root number. At later developmental stages, bacterial inoculation increased tiller formation by 7.4-fold and enhanced leaf development by 32%. In addition, UMJL46B synthesized gibberellic acid, significantly accelerating seed germination within 24 h and representing an unequivocal report of GA₃ production within the genus Flavobacterium. Finally, UMJL46B promoted root and shoot development in vitro through volatile mediated mechanisms, including acetoin and 3-methyl-butanol emission as complementary mechanisms by which UMJL46B enhances plant growth. The integration of genomic and functional analyses identifies F. johnsoniae UMJL46B as a plant growth-promoting endophyte and demonstrates the value of genome guided strategies for predicting beneficial plant microbe interactions.

Microbiological Research.title: An engineered probiotic yeast converts extracellular ATP into adenosine to alleviate experimental colitis.
Microbiological Research.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic relapsing intestinal disorder characterized by mucosal inflammation, epithelial barrier disruption, and gut microbial dysbiosis. Excessive extracellular ATP (eATP) accumulates in inflamed intestinal tissues and amplifies immune activation through purinergic signaling, whereas adenosine generated from extracellular nucleotide metabolism exerts immunoregulatory effects. Here, we engineered the probiotic yeast Saccharomyces boulardii to sense eATP and convert it into adenosine through a CRISPR-engineered dual-enzyme pathway consisting of apyrase and 5'-nucleotidase. The engineered strain showed ATP-responsive pathway activation and efficiently generated adenosine from eATP, allowing extracellular nucleotide metabolism to be modulated in inflammatory settings. Oral administration of this strain significantly alleviated disease severity in acute dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis and showed beneficial effects in a repeated-DSS model, improved barrier-related epithelial features, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine production, and supported mucosal recovery. Integrated microbiome and transcriptome analyses further showed partial restoration of gut microbial community structure, partial recovery of predicted microbial purine-related pathways, and attenuation of mucosal T-cell activation. Together, these findings indicate that engineered Saccharomyces boulardii can regulate extracellular purine metabolism in the inflamed gut and provide a microbial strategy for modulating intestinal inflammation.
